summary: Action cards are the next steps from the Sales CRM template's forecast: a row of cards, each saying what is waiting (submit the Q4 commit, move 4 close dates, send 4 follow-ups) with a button that opens it, beside a small picture of what that button leads to. In each picture a pointer glides to the item in focus and presses it, the item changes, and the list scrolls on to the next.
use: When an agent has work ready for a person to look at, and each piece should lead straight to where it is done.
On a dashboard or an overview, above the detail, so the few things that need someone come first.
When a picture of what the button opens helps people decide where to start.
Not for a long list of tasks: a table or Agent inbox holds those.
features: Three cards, each with a title, one muted line and a white outlined button. The buttons show their hover and press; what they open is yours to wire up.

Each picture is a short list: the item in focus is a window, its neighbours grey slips above and below. A rep's commit ticks in, a new date turns green as it is approved, and a draft turns from Drafted to Sent.
The three pictures run at different speeds, so they never move together, and the list wraps round without a jump.
While a mouse rests on the cards their pictures hold where they are, and carry on when it leaves. With reduced motion the pictures stay still on their first item.
Three across from 900px wide; below that the cards go one under another, the picture beside the words.

In React, `ActionCards` takes `cards`, each with its `title`, `detail`, `action` label, `onAction` and a `picture`: `commit` with team names, `dates` with each deal's old and new date, or `follow` with account names.
a11y: The pictures are `aria-hidden`: the title, the line under it and the button say everything.
The buttons are real buttons, reached with Tab in reading order.
With reduced motion turned on, nothing in the pictures moves.

faq.q: Can I have two cards or four?
faq.a: Yes. In React pass as many `cards` as you need; the row keeps three across and the rest wrap. In HTML add or remove a `.axc-c` card.

faq.q: Can a card have no picture?
faq.a: The picture is what tells these cards apart from a plain notice. For a line of text with a button, Banner fits better.

faq.q: Why does the picture stop while I hover?
faq.a: So it never moves while someone reads it or reaches for the button. It carries on as soon as the pointer leaves.
